body:
I think the ASVS currently lacks a requirement that states that you should perform access control or authorisation checks at all. I would expect requirement 4.1.1 to be something like:

> Verify that functionality is only accessible by users that are authorised to use that functionality.

This is implied in many of the requirements in chapter 4, but I think it would be valuable to make this its own requirement. If an application is missing an authorisation check, I want to be able to point to an ASVS requirement that specifies that every function should have access control, without necessarily including least privilege principle or trusted service layers.

comments.body:
Hey there. 4.1.3 captures the POLP principle well.

4.1.3 Verify that the principle of least privilege exists - users should only be able to access functions, data files, URLs, controllers, services, and other resources, for which they possess specific authorization. This implies protection against spoofing and elevation of privilege.

From the original issue point of view - I don't think we need another requirement for "verify that permission checks are there".
For me there are many duplicates in V4 category, but maybe I have not analyzed them enough yet.

Before deleting 1.4.3 or 4.1.3 (but I think it should be separate issue) it would be nice to know, why one of them is in architecture category and another in authorization category - maybe there is some good reason and instead of deleting it requires improvement in wording.

I think architecture is redundant, I can’t see why we need both.
